Each time, I was put on hold for nearly half an hour, only to be told that there were no available appointments—except for one over 20 days later.
I then called NHS 111, who advised me to contact my GP again. When I did, they said there was nothing they could do and suggested I go to a walk-in centre far from my home, despite the fact that I can barely walk.
When I finally got to the walk-in centre, the staff were helpful, but they told me I needed to go back to my GP to arrange an MRI. Now, nearly 15 days after my injury, I am still struggling to get the care I need. This experience has been incredibly frustrating and disappointing.
The appointment system is very inconvenient. Having to take time off work just for a 30-minute phone call is unnecessary and could easily be sorted with a simple online booking GPs at this practice are the reason many stay, but the behaviour of some reception staff is extremely unprofessional. If someone cannot speak to patients with basic courtesy, telephone manners or empathy, they should not be in a frontline role dealing with vulnerable people.

There is a clear lack of compassion when patients call for help, and it feels like reception staff do not want to assist at all. This is especially unacceptable when dealing with disabled patients who rely on clear communication and support.
